entries.author: A
entries.text: A bid far below the others is a trap — it means change-orders later, cut corners, or a contractor who misread the job.

entries.author: A
entries.text: Skipping permits is never worth it, even for small jobs — unpermitted work poisons resale and insurance, and I've seen it firsthand.

entries.author: A
entries.text: I should never hand a contractor a large sum upfront — a modest deposit, then payments tied to completed milestones.

entries.author: A
entries.text: Homeowners should never touch electrical or plumbing themselves — painting and demolition fine, but the trades exist for a reason.

entries.author: A
entries.text: Neighbors might skip permits, but that doesn't make it right; I've seen the consequences.

entries.author: A
entries.text: A good milestone schedule involves a small deposit, then payments after demo, rough-in, and finish.
